title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/16/2026
Reason for Admission: Sepsis and pneumonia.

Vitals:
T: 101.2 F, HR: 92, BP: 118/74, RR: 20, SpO2: 94% on RA.

Recent Labs:
WBC: 14.5k, Hgb: 13.2, Plt: 210k, Cr: 1.1, Na: 138, K: 4.0.

Review of Systems:
Resp: Productive cough, SOB. Fev: + (crackles).
CV: + (tachycardia).
GI: - (no N/V).
Neuro: - (alert/oriented).
Skin: - (no rashes).

Social History:
Retired. Lives with wife. Non-smoker. No alcohol.

Family History:
Father: HTN. Mother: DM2.

Hospital Course:
Pt is an 85-year-old male admitted with sepsis secondary to pneumonia. Pt presented with productive cough and fever. Initial workup showed elevated WBC. Blood cultures were performed; however, they grew no organism. Pt remained stable throughout admission. No acute organ dysfunction occurred during the stay. Managed with IV antibiotics and supplemental oxygen as needed. Pt showed significant improvement in respiratory status and afebrile on day 4. Transitioned to oral medications before discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Sepsis
2. Pneumonia

Discharge Medications:
1. Amoxicillin 500mg TID x 7 days
2. Guaifenesin 600mg PRN cough
3. Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours PRN fever/pain

Follow-up:
F/u with primary care physician in 1 week for re-evaluation of respiratory status and repeat labs.

Electronically signed, A. Rivera, MD, 05/16/2026
explanations: Sepsis with no organism identified and no organ dysfunction: A41.9 only (HCC 2).

distractors.why: No acute organ dysfunction is documented: no R65.2- code.
